title: Why every flow at 06:00 stops scaling
description: A 24-second explanation of concurrency saturation, queue growth, cascading failure, and staggered recovery.

accessibility.label: Animated explanation of scheduling collisions
accessibility.longDescription: Ten flows fit within execution capacity. As fifty and then more than two hundred sources target 06:00, capacity fills, a queue grows, timeouts retry together, and failures cascade. Staggered schedules, backoff with jitter, and failure isolation restore stable throughput.

scenes.title: Ten flows
scenes.narration: With ten sources, every flow can start at six and finish smoothly.

scenes.title: Growth
scenes.narration: At fifty sources, the same schedule creates competition for limited capacity.

scenes.title: Collision
scenes.narration: Beyond two hundred sources, the six o'clock spike overwhelms every execution slot.

scenes.title: Queue growth
scenes.narration: The queue grows, leaving less time for each connector to complete.

scenes.title: Cascade
scenes.narration: Timeouts retry together, turning one bottleneck into a cascading failure.

scenes.title: Stagger
scenes.narration: Dependency-aware staggering removes the single execution spike.

scenes.title: Isolate
scenes.narration: Backoff and jitter spread retries, while circuit breakers isolate unhealthy sources.

scenes.title: Stable throughput
scenes.displayText: Bounded work. Visible failures. Stable output.
scenes.narration: The system now operates within capacity and makes remaining failures visible.

reducedMotionSteps: At 10 sources, all scheduled work fits within the 20 available execution slots.
At 50 sources, 30 jobs queue; at more than 200, the queue dominates the run window.
Timeouts and synchronized retries amplify the bottleneck into cascading failure.
Staggering, backoff with jitter, and circuit breakers restore bounded, stable execution.
